name: Arctic Peeper
visual: Large eye, cool colours and luminous fins.
note: Existing sprite: move from freshwater 3.

name: Blinky
visual: Three eyes and an orange body; a very clear visual signature.
note: Existing sprite: move from alien.

name: Magikarp
visual: Whiskers, crown fin and bold orange scales.
note: Strong side profile; easy to distinguish from ordinary carp.

name: Cheep Cheep
visual: Original 16-bit red Cheep Cheep: compact body, white belly and yellow fins.
note: Use the SNES palette and sprite silhouette as the design reference, not the modern 3D model.

name: Nemo
visual: Orange clownfish with white bands and a smaller fin.
note: Expressive eyes and fin asymmetry must distinguish him from existing clownfish.

name: Dory
visual: Blue body, dark markings and a bright yellow tail.
note: Needs her expression to stand apart from the existing blue tang.

name: Flounder
visual: Yellow body, blue stripes and a rounded friendly face.
note: Use the animated design; very readable colours.

name: Cleo
visual: Golden body, long flowing fins and expressive eyelashes.
note: A classic goldfish option; face details matter at small scale.

name: Klaus
visual: Orange goldfish with a distinctive expressive face.
note: Use the fish without its bowl; face matters more than body shape.

name: Pudge
visual: Round orange body, blue spots and a little peanut-butter sandwich.
note: The sandwich is an optional identifying prop; the fish itself has a clean swimming silhouette.

name: Bubbles
visual: Bright yellow tang with large, wide-set eyes.
note: A familiar, simple fish shape; distinguish it from the existing yellow tang through its face.

name: Bloat
visual: Rounded pufferfish with a pale belly and small spines.
note: Adds a compact, chunky silhouette; reference shows the character rather than a generic puffer.

name: Deb
visual: Broad blue-and-white stripes and expressive eyes.
note: Different silhouette from Nemo and Dory, though it adds another Finding Nemo character.

name: Gurgle
visual: Purple front, yellow tail and large expressive eyes.
note: Strong colour contrast; must remain distinct from the existing royal gramma.

name: Mr. Ray
visual: Wide, spotted fins and a long slender tail.
note: Adds a gliding ray shape instead of another oval fish.

name: Destiny
q: Destiny Finding Dory whale shark character
visual: Large spotted blue body and a wide friendly mouth.
note: Would be scaled down into a tank-sized whale shark.

name: Mrs. Puff
visual: Round spotted pufferfish, sailor cap and blue collar.
note: Keep the cap and collar; adapt the upright pose into a swimmer.

name: Milo
visual: Pale green striped body, blue hair-like fin and orange lips.
note: Very expressive cartoon face; adapt the upright pose to swimming.

name: Bea Goldfishberg
visual: Golden striped body, long red hair and a star hair clip.
note: The red hair would make the silhouette distinctive at tank scale.

name: Oscar
visual: Green striped body and a large curly hair silhouette.
note: This is Oscar from Fish Hooks, not the rejected Oscar from Shark Tale.

name: Blipper
visual: Red fish wearing blue goggles; Kirby Super Star sprite.
note: A simple 16-bit design whose goggles provide a strong identity.

name: Chopper
visual: Red robotic fish with metal fins and a toothed mouth.
note: A mechanical alternative to organic fish; use the classic Sonic design.

name: Rip Van Fish
q: Rip Van Fish Super Mario World sprite
visual: Sleepy blue fish with orange lips and fins.
note: Original Super Mario World SNES sprite; retain the sleepy expression.

name: Porcu-Puffer
q: Porcu Puffer Super Mario World SNES sprite
visual: Blue puffer body, white spikes and pink-red lips.
note: Original Super Mario World SNES sprite and colours; no modern 3D redesign.

name: Fish Bone
q: Fish Bone Super Mario World SNES sprite
visual: White skeletal fish with a large eye and pointed teeth.
note: Original Super Mario World SNES sprite; a compact spooky option.

name: Blurp
visual: Green fish with white belly and a rounded, blunt head.
note: Original Super Mario World SNES sprite; close relative visually to Cheep Cheep.

name: Bitesize
visual: Small green fish with a large eye and pink-red tail.
note: Original Donkey Kong Country SNES sprite; a lively, compact shape.

name: Prego
visual: Round golden-orange fish with red fins and a blue scarf.
note: Original game screenshot; the scarf and broad body carry the identity.

name: Seaman
visual: Fish body with a human face and a forehead stalk.
note: A deliberately uncanny candidate from the Dreamcast virtual-pet game.
